import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1199

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1199](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1199)
- [Hi79] Hindman, Neil, Partitions and sums of integers with repetition.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1979), 19--32.
- [Ow74] J. Owings, E2494. Amer. Math. Monthly (1974), 902.
-/

open Pointwise

namespace Erdos1199

/--
Is it true that in any 2-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there exists an infinite set $A$
such that all elements of $A+A$ are the same colour?

A conjecture of Owings [Ow74].
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1199 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (color : ℕ → Fin 2), ∃ (A : Set ℕ),
    A.Infinite ∧ ∀ n ∈ (A+A), ∀ m ∈ (A+A), color n = color m := by
  sorry

/--
Hindman [Hi79] has shown that this is false for 3-colourings.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/HowieHwong/lean-erdos-proofs/blob/b8b641ba2d00dc4d1fe205a078a4159372672459/Erdos/P1199.lean#L85"]
theorem erdos_1199.variants.three :
    ∃ (color : ℕ → Fin 3), ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
    A.Infinite → ∃ n ∈ (A+A), ∃ m ∈ (A+A), color n ≠ color m := by
  sorry

end Erdos1199

reformulations.difference: The explicit restatement in Hindman–Leader–Strauss uses positive integers and defines two-colourings to use exactly two colours. Lean allows zero and unused colours, and expresses monochromaticity by equality of every two sum colours.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Deleting zero from an infinite witness preserves infinitude and only shrinks its sumset; positive-domain colourings can be extended arbitrarily at zero. A non-surjective map into Fin 2 is constant and therefore automatically has an infinite monochromatic-sumset witness. Finally, A.Infinite makes A+A nonempty, so pairwise equality of its colours is equivalent to the existence of a single colour shared by all a+b, including a=b. These equivalences were proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: Lean expresses the negative three-colour result through an explicit countercolouring and differently coloured sum witnesses; it also allows zero and does not require the colouring to be surjective.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Classically negating the universal monochromatic-sumset assertion gives exactly the Lean quantifiers. Applying the countercolouring to A without zero shows that the positive-integer convention is immaterial. A countercolouring using at most three colours can be made surjective by assigning all three colours to finitely many initial integers: for any infinite A, pass to an infinite tail whose sums avoid those changes. The negation, positivity and surjectivity equivalences were checked in Lean.

sources_consulted: Hindman, Leader and Strauss, Pairwise sums in colourings of the reals, Abh. Math. Semin. Univ. Hambg. 87 (2017), 275–287; author's manuscript, Introduction pp. 2–3 and references [4], [7]: https://nhindman.us/research/unctble.pdf

review.notes: Both declarations agree with the explicit account in Hindman–Leader–Strauss (2017), which cites both original references. Source-access limitation: erdosproblems.com returned Cloudflare challenges, the original Owings issue required authorization, and Hindman's original publisher text was blocked. The live companion database lists problem 1199 as open; the problem page's current status could not be checked directly. The exact cited three-colour proof compiled independently against installed Mathlib, with only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound as axioms. Scratch checks confirmed that pointwise addition includes repeated summands, excluded empty/singleton infinite witnesses, and proved the reported equivalences without sorry. The target file's hash matches the requested commit; all review artifacts are under /workspace/review/.
